subject: Post-demo: NatBank auth ops handoff and rotation plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Li <sophie.li@natbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: NatBank auth ops handoff and rotation plan

Hi Sophie — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so your team has something to review: 

1) Recommended auth options (short list):
   - Short-lived service accounts + workload identity federation (recommended for Prod)
   - OAuth 2.0 client flow for users needing delegated access to NatBank systems
   - Scoped API keys for internal tooling / low-risk workloads (rotate frequently, restricted scopes)

2) Key rotation / governance:
   - Propose 30-day automatic rotation for short-lived tokens; 90-day for service account keys where rotation is manual
   - Integrate with your KMS (we support Google KMS / AWS KMS / customer HSM) and provide rotation hooks

3) SDK & routing setup:
   - We’ll provide a starter repo (Node + Python) with built-in token refresh + retry logic
   - Route by policy: latency-sensitive calls to Dedicated pool; cost-sensitive batch calls to hosted model variants

4) Structured outputs & reranker usage:
   - If you plan to use tool-calling or structured JSON responses, we’ll include schema validation examples in the SDK
   - Embeddings + rerankers: suggest a separate ingest pipeline and a cached prefix store to keep inference cost predictable

Attachments: integration-checklist.xlsx (initial checklist), natbank-security-questionnaire.pdf (answers draft)

Next steps: can we book an "Auth Ops + Rotation" 60-minute follow-up with your security/infra folks? Proposed times: Thu 8/13 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 8/14 9:00–10:00 PT. 

If those work, I’ll share a quick agenda and a Drive folder with the starter SDK and runbook.

Thanks —
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Sophie Li <sophie.li@natbank.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: NatBank Security <security@natbank.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: NatBank auth ops handoff and rotation plan

Ben — thanks for the detailed recap, this is helpful. A few clarifying items from security and infra: 

- For Prod we prefer short-lived credentials backed by our HSM / on-prem KMS — can Redwood support a token-exchange pattern where our KMS mints ephemeral credentials for calls into the Redwood Private deployment?
- We need the exact fields you expect in the service-account JWT (audience, scope, custom claims). Can you provide a sample JWT payload?
- Regarding rotation cadence: our policy requires no long-lived plaintext keys in S3/DBs; can your SDK avoid persisting service account private keys and instead use a local signer/agent?

Also, security has a few follow-ups and attached a questionnaire (see attached inlined PDF). Can you confirm who will own the security responses on your side?

Sophie Li
Product Security Manager | NatBank
sophie.li@natbank.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Li <sophie.li@natbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, NatBank Security <security@natbank.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: NatBank auth ops handoff and rotation plan

Sophie — great questions. Quick answers inline, plus next steps and an initial handoff owner: 

- Token-exchange pattern: yes. For Redwood Private we support a token-exchange where your KMS mints short-lived credentials (STS-style) and exchanges them for an ephemeral Redwood token via our token broker. We can provide the token-broker container for on-prem or run it in your VPC.

- Sample JWT payload: attached below (example service_account_claims.json) — highlight fields: iss (your KMS service identity), aud (https://private.redwood.internal/token-exchange), exp (short expiry), sub (service-account@natbank), scopes (list of allowed APIs).

- SDK key handling: our official SDKs avoid persisting long-lived private keys. We'll add a local signer integration (agent) that uses your HSM via PKCS#11 or a short-lived gRPC signer that only holds keys in memory.

Attachments included in this thread: integration-checklist.xlsx, natbank-security-questionnaire.pdf

Ownership: Marissa Cole (Solutions Engineering) will be the main handoff owner for technical responses and runbook delivery. Stephanie Nguyen (Product PM) will own the rotation policy docs and test plan. 

Proposed workshop: "Auth Ops + SDK deep-dive" — 60 minutes — suggested invitees: NatBank security, infra, dev platform. Confirm whether Thu 8/13 10:00 PT or Fri 8/14 9:00 PT works; we can do remote or on-site in SF.

Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: NatBank auth ops handoff and rotation plan

Hi Sophie — Marissa here. Thanks for the questions — happy to own technical delivery. A few addenda from the Solutions team before the workshop: 

- Reranker / embeddings note: if you intend to use embeddings + reranker for search ranking (sensitive PII), we recommend a separate encrypted vector store with per-tenant encryption keys. We can demonstrate the flow (ingest -> embed -> index -> rerank) in the workshop and show how auth scopes are scoped at the pipeline layer.

- Tool-calling / structured output: we’ll include example JSON schemas and a validation step in the SDK so your engineers can opt into strict parsing (fail-fast on extra fields).

- Drive link with starter repo & runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Cnatbank-arch — contains:
   * starter-node-sdk (token refresh + local signer)
   * starter-python-sdk (requests + retry middleware)
   * runbook-auth-ops.md (rotation playbook + test checklist)

I’ll send calendar invite for Fri 8/14 09:00 PT and include a short agenda. If you prefer Thu, we can swap.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
